Admitting Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Hospital Course:

The patient was admitted post-SIRT after whole-body 18-fluorine-fluorodeoxyglucose positron-emission-tomography/computed tomography (18F-FDG PET/CT) revealed malignant lesions in the medial segment of the left hepatic lobe, following left lateral segmentectomy that had been performed. The patient was referred to our hospital as there were no local options of stereotactic ablative radiation therapy.

During the course of follow-up, the patient developed progressive dyspnea and dry cough three weeks post-SIRT. Chest radiogram and computed tomography of the thorax were performed, and the patient put on intravenous prednisone at 1 mg/Kg/day with antibiotic therapy. Seven weeks post-SIRT, 18F-FDG PET/CT scan appeared to show multiple ground-glass opacities in both lungs compatible with radiation pneumonitis. The patient was rehospitalized and glucocorticoid treatment with modified antibiotherapy continued. Four weeks post-SIRT, DLCO reduction was more remarkable and the SpO2 level dropped to 97%.

Eleven weeks post-SIRT, a CT scan revealed bilateral diffuse, patchy ground-glass attenuation/consolidation areas seemed to have progressed, along with a significant decrease in SpO2 from 92 to 82%. The patient was transferred to the Intensive Care Unit (ICU), and one week later, the patient expired due to pulmonary complications.

Discharge Medications:

None.

Follow-up:

The patient expired during Hospitalization. 

Discharge Condition:

Deceased.

text:
# ICD-10-AM Principal Diagnosis: **J70.0 – Acute pulmonary manifestations due to radiation**

## Rationale

The condition that occasioned the admission (rehospitalisation) and drove the hospital course, including ICU transfer and death, was **radiation pneumonitis** following selective internal radiation therapy (SIRT, Y-90 radioembolisation).

- Progressive dyspnoea and dry cough began about 3 weeks post-SIRT.
- PET/CT showed bilateral ground-glass opacities compatible with radiation pneumonitis.
- DLCO and SpO2 declined despite glucocorticoids and antibiotics.
- The patient died from pulmonary complications.

**Acute vs. chronic:** J70.0 (radiation pneumonitis) applies rather than J70.1 (chronic and other pulmonary manifestations due to radiation, e.g., post-radiation fibrosis). The presentation was pneumonitis evolving over weeks, not established fibrosis.

## Suggested Additional Codes

| Code | Description |
|------|-------------|
| **Y84.2** | Radiological procedure and radiotherapy as the cause of abnormal reaction of the patient, or of later complication, without mention of misadventure at the time of the procedure |
| **Y92.22** | Place of occurrence: health service area |
| **C22.x / C78.7** | Liver malignancy. Assign C22.0 if hepatocellular carcinoma, or C78.7 if secondary, plus the primary site. The documentation does not specify which, so query the clinician. |
| **Z90.4x** | Acquired absence of part of the digestive tract (prior left lateral segmentectomy), if applicable per local standards |
| **J96.0x** | Acute respiratory failure, if documented by the clinician (SpO2 82%, ICU transfer) |

**Note:** Confirm the tumour histology and whether respiratory failure is documented before finalising the secondary codes.
